question: For which of the following patients would you recommend prophylaxis against mycobacterium avium-intracellulare?

options.opa: 22-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 750 cells/ microliter and a viral load of 500,000 copies/mL
options.opb: 30-year old HIV positive male with CD4 count of 20 cells/ microliter and a viral load of < 50 copies/mL
options.opc: 45-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 250 cells/ microliter and a viral load of 100,000 copies/mL
options.opd: 50-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 150 cells/ microliter and a viral load of < 50 copies/mL
options.ope: 36-year old HIV positive male with CD4 count of 75 cells/microliter and an undetectable viral load.

analysis: Prophylaxis against Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare is recommended for HIV-infected individuals with a CD4 count less than 50 cells/microliter. This is typically indicated for patients with severe immunosuppression.
